neighbours.label: relative 'that' after a noun in descriptive natural-history / anatomy prose (nests that hang, folds that cover)
fire: The spiders weave sticky webs that stretch between the low shrubs.
In autumn the moths spin pale cocoons that cling to the undersides of leaves.
Beneath the skin lies a thin membrane that wraps around each muscle.
The coral forms branching colonies that shelter thousands of small fish.
Wasps build papery chambers that hang from the eaves of barns.
The plant sends out long runners that root wherever they touch soil.
Each kidney has a fibrous capsule that protects its delicate tissue.
The beetle larvae dig narrow tunnels that wind through the bark.
quiet: The spiders weave sticky webs between the low shrubs at night.
In autumn the moths spin pale cocoons on the undersides of leaves.
Beneath the skin lies a thin membrane around each muscle.
The coral forms branching colonies, sheltering thousands of small fish.
Wasps build papery chambers under the eaves of barns.
The plant sends out long runners, rooting wherever they touch soil.
Each kidney has a fibrous capsule protecting its delicate tissue.
The beetle larvae dig narrow tunnels through the soft bark.
